newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. warns Afghan Taleban on suppressing women.
newsitem.headline: U.N. warns Afghan Taleban on suppressing women.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Monday told U.N. agencies to respect equal rights for women in Afghanistan and warned the country's radical Islamic militia, Taleban, that discrimination could seriously affect relief programmes.
"We have decided to restate our single, system-wide policy on the question of gender equality," he said in a statement sent to the many U.N. agencies operating in Afghanistan.
He said that the agencies had to respect any requirements from donors as well as recipients providing they "do not conflict with our stated principles."
This meant cooperation with authorities "but at the same time, the U.N. system is obliged to be guided by the norms and requirements stated in the (U.N.) Charter," he said.

Restrictions reported to date, such as denying women employment and education, could "have serious repercussions on the ability of the United Nations to deliver programmes of relief and reconstruction," he warned.

U.N. officials said one purpose of the statement was to back up relief agencies who are dealing with the Taleban in various regions and make sure their policies are uniform throughout the country. Some have already stopped funding schools after girls last year were forced to drop out.

With the Taleban having captured the capital of Kabul last month, women, many of them war widows, were forbidden to work or attend school or university. Some were beaten on the streets for not being dressed properly.

Boutros-Ghali said that Ivanka Corti, the head of the U.N. Committee for the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women, had expressed alarm at reports of discrimination to date, saying the restrictions were a violation of international treaties which Afghanistan had signed.

The United Nations also has a political mission in Afghanistan led by Norbert Holl of Germany. According to U.N. Assistant Secretary Rosario Green, a woman will assume one of the vacant posts on the mission if the group continues functioning in Afghanistan.
